results.claim: THEORY.md, R1. Standard-model data bound with no condition-dependent accuracy loss

human: H-LB-data: Woodworth–Srebro, arXiv:1605.08003v1, Theorem 8, registered iteration conversion
H-LB-zsh: Zhang–Shu–He, arXiv:2010.08766v2, Theorem 3.1 and Section 4.1
H-LB-net: Scaman et al., arXiv:1702.08704v1, Theorems 1–2
comparison.explanation: On the registered class, keeps the data startup term and replaces log(R sqrt(nm/kappa)) by log R, with validity down to a constant R. The improvement is unbounded at the same accuracy inside H-LB-data's range when kappa/(nm) and m/n grow. The proof does not extend the original unrestricted algorithm or component proximal oracle theorem.

results.claim: THEORY.md, R2. Smooth local averages alone do not preserve the H-UB order

human: H-UB: Liu–Low, arXiv:2402.02356v1, Theorem 5.1 and Corollary 5.3
H-LB-avg: Zhou–Gu, arXiv:1901.11224v1, Theorem 4.1 (distinct mean-squared assumption)
comparison.explanation: Necessity result: no algorithm can retain the registered H-UB order after replacing individual smoothness by only L-smooth local averages and still tuning the target order with that L. Formal separation includes any fixed powers of logarithms. The two bounds themselves are about different classes.

results.claim: THEORY.md, R3. Matching two-node bounds by exact averaging and proximal acceleration

human: H-UB: Liu–Low, arXiv:2402.02356v1, Theorem 5.1 and Corollary 5.3
Scaman et al., arXiv:1702.08704v1, Section 3.2 and discussion after Corollary 1
comparison.explanation: Two-node matching bound in the local-average-only relaxation and the standard m=1 case. Exact decoding from a weighted sum removes dependence on the spectral gap and uses one round per accelerated step, but a full local gradient per step can worsen the data count at large m.

results.claim: THEORY.md, R4. Removing connectivity can make the averaged-output problem unsolvable

human: H-UB: Liu–Low, arXiv:2402.02356v1, doubly stochastic matrix assumption and Theorem 5.1
H-LB-net: Scaman et al., arXiv:1702.08704v1, Theorem 2
comparison.explanation: An explicit support-based impossibility for the evaluator's averaged output if the matrix class is weakened to permit the identity. Not a stronger finite-rho network lower bound.
